name: Kappa Stream-Only Architecture
tagline: Treating an append-only distributed log as the single source of truth for both real-time streaming and historical offset-0 replay.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of Kappa architecture—from eliminating Lambda's dual batch/stream drift to Blue/Green offset-0 replays, Kafka Tiered Storage, and RocksDB state TTLs.

spark.summary: Kappa architecture eliminates the separate batch layer of Lambda architecture by treating an append-only distributed log as the single source of truth for both real-time processing and historical replay.
spark.keyTakeaway: One code path, one immutable log: when business logic changes, you spin up a second stream job from offset 0, backfill a new serving table, and atomically swap pointers.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Lambda architecture forces teams to write and reconcile two separate codebases (e.g., Spark SQL for batch + Flink for real-time), guaranteeing semantic drift between yesterday's dashboard and today's.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Immutable Kafka Log (Live + Tiered S3) -> Flink v1/v2 -> Atomic View Swap (Kafka + Tiered S3 Log -> Flink Stream Job v2 -> Serving Table v1 -> Serving Table v2); Zero-Downtime Offset-0 Backfill & Serving Alias Swap (Kafka + S3 Tiered -> Flink job-v2 -> Serving view_v2 -> Query Alias).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Explore late-data watermarking, Kafka exactly-once fencing, and how Kappa contrasts with Lambda. Replaying 30 days of Kafka events at 500k events/sec will DDoS your serving database if written live.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore late-data watermarking, Kafka exactly-once fencing, and how Kappa contrasts with Lambda.

learningJourney.title: What is Kappa Architecture
learningJourney.explanation:
Lambda architecture forces teams to write and reconcile two separate codebases (e.g., Spark SQL for batch + Flink for real-time), guaranteeing semantic drift between yesterday's dashboard and today's. **Kappa Architecture** (Jay Kreps) deletes the batch layer.

An immutable partitioned log (**Kafka** with `retention.ms=-1` or **Tiered Storage** to S3/GCS, or **Apache Pulsar**) is the **Single Source of Truth**. One stream codebase (Flink / Kafka Streams) handles both live tailing and historical backfills using **event-time watermarks**.

sectionDiagram.title: Immutable Kafka Log (Live + Tiered S3) -> Flink v1/v2 -> Atomic View Swap

cards.label: Zero Drift
cards.detail: Live metrics and historical backfills execute the exact same Flink/Kafka Streams code.

cards.label: Tiered Storage
cards.detail: Old Kafka segments offload to S3 (~$0.023/GB-mo) instead of expensive broker NVMe.

cards.label: Isolated Replay
cards.detail: job-v2 writes to view_v2 in isolation; serving alias swaps only after catching up to live tail.

sectionDiagram.summary: Treating the distributed log as SSOT lets you fix bugs via Blue/Green stream replay without maintaining a separate batch engine.

learningJourney.title: Why Blue/Green Replay & Determinism Matter
learningJourney.explanation: When a double-counting bug is discovered in a surge-pricing pipeline, engineers deploy `surge-v2` with a fresh consumer group starting 14 days back in Kafka Tiered Storage into `view_v2`, let it catch up to the live tail, and atomically swap the serving alias—zero downtime and zero batch rewrite.

learningJourney.title: Bounded RocksDB State TTL & Idempotent Watermark Config
learningJourney.explanation: Prevent unbounded RocksDB state growth by configuring `StateTtlConfig` on keyed descriptors and enabling incremental RocksDB checkpoints to S3.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```java
// Flink StateTtlConfig + Idleness Watermark preventing RocksDB bloat & watermark stalls
StateTtlConfig ttlConfig = StateTtlConfig
    .newBuilder(Time.days(30))
    .setUpdateType(StateTtlConfig.UpdateType.OnCreateAndWrite)
    .setStateVisibility(StateTtlConfig.StateVisibility.NeverReturnExpired)
    .cleanupInRocksdbCompactFilter(1000)
    .build();

WatermarkStrategy<Event> wm = WatermarkStrategy
    .<Event>forBoundedOutOfOrderness(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
    .withTimestampAssigner((e, ts) -> e.eventTimeMs())
    .withIdleness(Duration.ofSeconds(30));
```

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Kappa vs. Lambda vs. Unified Lakehouse (Iceberg + Flink)
learningJourney.explanation: Compare stream-only Kappa against dual-pipeline Lambda and modern lakehouse streaming.

benefits: One codebase, zero batch/stream semantic drift, and fast Blue/Green offset replays.
costs: Reading old segments from S3 Tiered Storage adds API/egress cost during huge replays.

benefits: Leverages specialized batch SQL for petabyte historical joins while keeping speed state tiny.
costs: Maintaining two codebases causes 10–15% metric drift at batch/speed boundaries.

benefits: Flink streams into Iceberg; Spark/Trino runs ad-hoc batch SQL on the exact same ACID tables.
costs: Requires scheduled Iceberg compaction to avoid small-file proliferation.

learningJourney.explanation: Replaying 30 days of Kafka events at 500k events/sec will DDoS your serving database if written live. Always write `job-v2` to an isolated `view_v2` index with sink rate-limiting, then swap the read alias once lag hits zero.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why can a single idle Kafka partition stall event-time window outputs across an entire Apache Flink Kappa pipeline?

options.text: Because Flink's global operator watermark advances to `min(partition_watermarks)`, so an idle partition holds the watermark back unless `withIdleness()` is configured
options.feedback: Correct: `WatermarkStrategy.withIdleness()` marks quiet partitions idle so active partitions keep advancing.

options.text: Because RocksDB locks all partitions until every partition receives 1,000 events
options.feedback: RocksDB state is keyed independently; the stall is due to watermark progression.

options.text: Because Kafka Tiered Storage deletes idle partitions
options.feedback: Tiered Storage only offloads old closed segments to object storage.

beginner.byteSummary:
**The Core Idea (Beginner):** Lambda architecture forces teams to write and reconcile two separate codebases (e.g., Spark SQL for batch + Flink for real-time), guaranteeing semantic drift between yesterday's dashboard and today's.

**How It Flows:** Think of Kappa Stream-Only Architecture as a clear step-by-step chain: Kafka + Tiered S3 Log -> Flink Stream Job v2 -> Serving Table v1 -> Serving Table v2 -> Kafka + S3 Tiered.

**Why Beginners Should Care:** One code path, one immutable log: when business logic changes, you spin up a second stream job from offset 0, backfill a new serving table, and atomically swap pointers.
